skills.name: benchmarking
skills.description: Guide for building, running, and analyzing Nanvix performance benchmarks. Use this when asked about benchmark setup, execution, or interpretation.

skills.name: build
skills.description: Guide for building, formatting, linting, and spell-checking Nanvix with z. Use this when asked to build or validate the repository.

skills.name: ci-cd-pipeline
skills.description: Guide for Nanvix CI and GitHub Actions workflow behavior, including local pipeline execution and matrix coverage. Use this when asked about CI checks, workflow failures, or release flow.

skills.name: coding-standards
skills.description: Detailed Nanvix coding, documentation, and review standards across Rust, C/C++, Python, and Shell. Use this when asked to implement or review code quality conventions.

skills.name: daemon-development
skills.description: Guide for developing and debugging Nanvix daemons, including guest daemons and host linuxd behavior. Use this when asked about daemon architecture or daemon changes.

skills.name: gdb-debugging
skills.description: Guide for debugging Nanvix guests using GDB remote debugging over the microvm machine type. Use this when asked about attaching GDB, setting breakpoints, or stepping through kernel code.

skills.name: kernel-development
skills.description: Guide for modifying and debugging the Nanvix kernel architecture and kernel-call paths. Use this when asked about kernel internals or kernel implementation changes.

skills.name: library-development
skills.description: Guide for creating and modifying Nanvix libraries under src/libs, including guest no_std and host std crates. Use this when asked about library architecture or crate changes.

skills.name: test-development
skills.description: Guide for writing, running, and debugging Nanvix unit, integration, and system tests in Rust and C/C++. Use this when asked about test implementation or failures.

skills.name: test
skills.description: Guide for running Nanvix tests with z. Use this when asked to run unit tests, integration tests, or the full test suite.

skills.name: troubleshooting
skills.description: Guide for diagnosing Nanvix build, runtime, and test failures, including cleanup and debugging workflows. Use this when asked to investigate errors or unstable behavior.

skills.name: user-app-development
skills.description: Guide for developing, building, and running Nanvix user-space applications across supported runtimes and languages. Use this when asked about guest app implementation or execution.

skills.name: find-skills
skills.description: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.

skills.name: customize-cloud-agent
skills.description: Skill for customizing the Copilot cloud agent (formerly known as Copilot coding agent) environment, including copilot-setup-steps.yml configuration, preinstalling tools and dependencies, runners, and settings. Use when the user mentions copilot-setup-steps, copilot setup steps, or wants to configure the cloud agent environment.

53. `table.rs:231-237`:

55. #[verus_spec(
56.     requires index@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
57.     ensures  spec_table_word(self@.addr, index@) == spec_entry_raw(entry),
58. )]
59. pub unsafe fn write(&self, index: TableIndex, entry: E) { ... }   // external_body
60. ```
61. 
62. `spec_table_word(addr, index)` is a **pure** `uninterp spec fn` — one fixed value
63. per `(addr, index)`. Because `write` is `external_body`, this `ensures` is
64. **assumed** at every call site. Pinning a *pure* function to a caller-chosen
65. `entry` makes the spec contradict itself across two writes to the same slot.
66. Concrete derivation a caller can perform (all facts are assumed/broadcast):
67. 
68. ```
69. write(i, e1)  ⟹  spec_table_word(a, i) == spec_entry_raw(e1)      [A1]
70. write(i, e2)  ⟹  spec_table_word(a, i) == spec_entry_raw(e2)      [A2]
71. A1, A2        ⟹  spec_entry_raw(e1) == spec_entry_raw(e2)
72. lemma_entry_roundtrip:
73.     spec_entry_from_raw(spec_entry_raw(e1)) == Some(e1)
74.     spec_entry_from_raw(spec_entry_raw(e2)) == Some(e2)
75.         ⟹  Some(e1) == Some(e2)  ⟹  e1 == e2
76. ```

78. `e1 == e2`, i.e. **`false`** — and from `false`, anything. This is a genuine
79. soundness hole, not a weak spec. It is latent today only because every upstream
80. caller starts with `proof! { admit(); }`; it becomes exploitable the moment a
81. real `write(i,e1); write(i,e2)` proof is attempted. The fixer's "scratch-crate"
82. check only exercised a *single* write (read-after-one-write), which is exactly
83. the case that hides this bug.
84.

86. `&self` and the model represents the cell as a **pure** function. A faithful
87. write-transition needs a state that changes between calls (`old@ -> @`), which
88. requires either `&mut self` (wrong for a non-owning handle, would cascade) or the
89. deferred ghost permission token (proving phase, cascades into the out-of-scope
90. `admit()` callers). This is precisely the *Open Mechanism Note* / *As-Built
91. Decision* in `view_design.md`: the write→`entries` transition must be deferred.
92. The fixer reintroduced the `entries` transition into `write`'s `ensures` via a
93. pure-function pin, which is the unsound shortcut that note warned against.
94. 
95. Note this does **not** condemn `read`: reading a pure accessor is sound (two
96. reads agree; matches `identity_map_view()`'s deferral). The defect is isolated to
97. `write` asserting an equality on the global accessor.

102. write→`entries` transition to the proving-phase ghost token, exactly as
103. `identity_map.spec.rs` defers `identity_map_view()`'s `v -> v'`.
104.

107. #[verus_verify(external_body)]
108. #[verus_spec(
109.     requires
110.         index@ < crate::mem::PAGE_TABLE_LENGTH,
111. )]
112. pub unsafe fn write(&self, index: TableIndex, entry: E) { ... }
113. ```
114. and update the trust-boundary comment to state that the slot-update transition
115. (`self@.entries[index@] == Some(entry)` after the call) is **deferred to the
116. proving-phase page-table permission token** (cite the `identity_map_view()`
117. deferral convention), so the omission is clearly intentional, not an oversight.
118. 
119. Keep unchanged (all sound): `read`'s `ensures`
120. (`result == spec_table_read::<E>(self@.addr, index@)`), the `raw`/`from_raw`
121. ensures, `lemma_entry_roundtrip`, and the `TableView { addr, entries }` view.
122. 
123. **Do NOT** instead try to "patch" by removing the round-trip lemma or by adding
124. raw-injectivity — those either drop a wanted caller guarantee (#10) or make the
125. contradiction *more* reachable. The correct move is to not pin a pure function in
126. `write`'s postcondition at all.
127. 
128. If you believe `write` can keep a **sound** contents postcondition without a
129. state token, that is a justification — prove it: write a scratch Verus client
130. that calls `write(i, e1); write(i, e2)` with `e1 != e2` (e.g. distinct via a
131. hypothesis), `broadcast use lemma_entry_roundtrip`, and `assert(false)`. If that

218.     /// Writes `entry` at `index`.

220.     /// # Safety
221.     ///
222.     /// The memory at `base + index * size_of::<PteWord>()` must be valid for a volatile write.
223.     ///
224.     // Trust boundary (see `tcb-allowed.md` / `verus-unsupported.md`): materializes a raw
225.     // `*mut PteWord` from the integer base address and performs a volatile store — the hardware
226.     // page-table write. The `usize -> *mut T` cast is unsupported by Verus, so the body cannot be
227.     // verified; same int-to-pointer boundary as `read`. The `ensures` pins the (trusted) global
228.     // page-table memory ghost at the written slot; because that ghost is a pure function, every
229.     // other slot/page is preserved across the call (the caller-facing frame condition), and a
230.     // subsequent `read(index)` decodes back to `Some(entry)` via `lemma_entry_roundtrip`.
231.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
232.     #[verus_spec(
233.         requires

237.     )]
